name: Bastard Brag
description: Bastard Brag is a lively variant of Three-Card Brag that mixes the hand rankings of Brag with the card-swapping mechanics of Commerce. Instead of a purely static hand, players are dealt three cards and share access to a 'Widow' hand on the table. Players take turns swapping cards with the Widow to improve their hand until someone 'Knocks' (stops the bus) or the pot reaches a certain limit. It is a game of speed, memory, and nerve.

overview.description: Bastard Brag is a lively variant of Three-Card Brag that mixes the hand rankings of Brag with the card-swapping mechanics of Commerce. history.origins: Evolved in British pubs as a faster, more interactive alternative to standard Brag. The inclusion of the 'Swap' mechanic aligns it with the 'Commerce' family of games (like 31 or Scat), but the use of Brag rankings gives it a distinct flavor.
timeline: Mid-20th Century: Appears in UK pub game compilations.
1990s: Becomes a popular 'warm-up' game for poker nights.
Present: Often played as 'Stop the Bus' in family settings using 31-scoring instead of Brag hands.
history.cultural: A classic 'start-stop' game where the tension builds simply by waiting for someone to knock.
history.evolution: The game has two distinct branches: the 'Lives' version (where the worst hand loses a life) and the 'Betting' version (closer to poker). The 'Lives' version is often synonymous with 'Stop the Bus'.

setup.dealing: Each player receives 3 cards face down. Three cards are dealt face up (or face down in some variants) to the center of the table (The Widow).
setup.equipment: Chips or tokens (3 Lives each for the Lives version).

rules.objective: Avoid having the lowest hand when the game stops (Lives version) or win the pot with the best hand (Betting version).
rules.gameplay: Players take turns clockwise. On your turn, you may: 1. **Swap One**: Trade one card from your hand with one card from the Widow. 2. **Swap All**: Trade your entire 3-card hand with the Widow. 3. **Pass/Knock**: If you are happy with your hand, you knock on the table.
keyRules: You cannot swap and knock in the same turn (usually).
Prial of 3s is the highest hand (Classic Brag rule).
Aces are high in runs (A-K-Q) but low in 3-2-A (Run) or A-2-3 (Running Flush) depending on house rules.

strategy.basic: Watch the Widow! If someone takes a card you needed, you know what they are building. Don't knock unless you have at least a Flush or a high Pair.
strategy.intermediate: The Defensive Swap: If there is a high card in the Widow (e.g., Ace of Spades) that doesn't help you, but you know the player next to you is collecting Spades, take it anyway to block them.
strategy.advanced: The Fake Knock: If playing the betting version, knock early with a mediocre hand to panic opponents into making sub-optimal swaps, forcing them to break potential hands.
tips: A Prial of 3s is instant gratificationâ€”if you notice 3s being passed around, hoard them.
In 'Lives', you don't need the best hand, you just need to beat the worst hand.

variations.name: Stop the Bus
variations.description: Identical mechanics but uses '31' scoring (suit sums) instead of Brag hands.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Stop the Bus is documented as a related 31-point variant; its scoring changes are not modeled as engine overrides yet.

variations.name: Bastard Brag (Betting)
variations.description: Standard Brag betting intervals occur after every round of swaps instead of an elimination knock.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: The betting version is described narratively; betting structure differences are not encoded as separate engine overrides.

scoring.winCondition: Be the last player with lives remaining.

synthesis.shortDescription: The classic pub game of swapping and surviving. Improve your 3-card hand using the communal 'Widow' cards, but watch out: once someone knocks, you have one turn left to save your life. Whether you play for cash or for pride, the Prial of 3s reigns supreme.

hero.tagline: Swap fast. Knock early. Don't be the last one on the bus.
